conversation.Statement: Good afternoon, this is Michael Turner with the IRS Taxpayer Assistance Center. Am I speaking with Alex Miller?
Yes, this is Alex. How can I help you?
I'm calling because our records show you're eligible for a federal tax refund due to recent stimulus adjustments. Have you already received any correspondence about your IRS refund status?
No, I haven't gotten anything about a refund. Is this about the taxes I filed last month?
Exactly, Alex. Because you're a first-time filer, some additional verification is needed before the IRS can release your $2,750 refund. We want to ensure there are no delays.
Oh, wow, I didn't know I was getting a refund. What do I need to do?
First, I need to confirm some information. Can you verify your date of birth and the last four digits of your Social Security number for me?
Uh, sure. My birthday is May 14, 2000, and the last four are 6789.
Thank you. Now, before your refund can be processed, the IRS requires a one-time clearance fee of $179 to ensure your identity and prevent fraudulent claims. This is standard for new taxpayers.
A fee? I didn't know there were fees for getting a refund. Is that normal?
Yes, this is a recent policy to combat increasing tax fraud. If not paid within 24 hours, your refund will be placed on indefinite hold and you may be flagged for audit.
I definitely don't want an audit. How do I pay the fee?
For your convenience, we accept clearance payments via Zelle, Cash App, or prepaid gift cards. Which method would you prefer?
I guess I could use Cash App. I have that on my phone.
Perfect. Please send the $179 fee to our IRS processing account, which is $FedClearance2024. After you send it, let me know so I can verify and finalize your refund.
Okay, I'll do it now. Is there anything else I have to do?
Just make sure the payment is completed within the next 30 minutes. If not, your refund will be seized and you may face a penalty for non-compliance.
Whoa, seized? That's a little scary. I really want to avoid any issues.
Yes, it's important to take care of it right away. The IRS takes identity verification very seriously, and failure to comply could result in a freeze on your tax account and further complications.
Alright, I understand. I'm sending the payment now.
Thank you, Alex. Once I receive confirmation, I'll process your refund immediately. Please let me know if you have any trouble with the payment.
